text: For the choir director. Of David. The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, their deeds are vile; there is no one who does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man to see if there are any who understand, any who seek God.

versions.text: The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of Adam to see if there are any who understand, any who seek God.
versions.explanation: "Children of Adam" is a possible rendering, but "children of man" (or "human race") is the ordinary sense of בְּנֵי־אָדָם here and reads more naturally aloud without implying a genealogical reference.

text: All have turned away, together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they know nothing, all these evildoers, who devour my people as they devour bread and never call on the LORD?
There they were seized with terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.

versions.text: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses a cognate accusative in the perfect ("they dreaded a dread"); "There they were seized with terror" preserves the past-tense force and the intensity of the idiom while reading well aloud.

text: You would frustrate the plans of the poor, but the LORD is their refuge.
Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
